<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 5:4:2">Y. Succ. V, 55ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>ולקִילּוּסָן הוא צריך</he> is he in need of their praise? <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 5:4:2">Ib.</cite> <he>חביב קילוסן של ישראל וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="S00969"><he>קילוסין</he></cite>) Israel’s praise (of the Lord) is preferred to &c.
<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 5">Lev. R. s. 5</cite>, end (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 19">Ps. XIX</cite>) <he>בתחלה משורר בק׳</he> he begins by singing praise.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 15">Ex. R. s. 15</cite> <he>הכל נותנין לי ק׳</he> all will do me homage; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="S00969"><he>קִילּוּסִין</he></cite>, <cite ref="S00959"><he>קִלּ׳</he></cite>. Y. Succ. l. c. <he>אע״פ שיש לפניו כמה ק׳ וכ׳</he> although there are before him many praises (<cite ref="Daniel 7:10">Dan. VII, 10</cite>), yet Israel’s praise &c., v. supra. Y. Pes. VIII, 36ᵇ; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 1:5:4">Y. M. Kat. I, 80ᵈ</cite> top <he>מהו דברים … ק׳</he> what words?… praises (of the departed whose bones are collected).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 16:1:7">Y. Sabb. XVI, 15ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>כל הק׳ שישראל מקלסין וכ׳</he> all the praises which Israel offers to the Lord (the psalms) correspond in number to the years of Jacob’s life; <cite ref="Tractate Soferim 16:11">Treat. Sof’rim XVI, 11</cite>. Y. R. Hash. IV, 59ᶜ <he>עשרה ק׳ וכ׳</he> ten praises (Halleluiahs) which David spoke (Bab.

<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 32a:17">ib. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>הילולים</he>); a. fr.—[<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 5">Gen. R. s. 5</cite> <he>נעשה ק׳ להקב״ה</he>, v. <cite ref="S01265"><he>קְלִוְוסִין</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 885:9">Yalk. Deut. 885</cite> <he>בקלוסין</he>, read: <he>בקולסין</he>, v. <cite ref="S00356"><he>קוֹלָס</he></cite>.]
M. Kat. 27ᵇ ק׳ ברגל ḳillus is done with the foot; Tosef. ib. II, 17 ק׳ זה פישוט וכ׳ (not קילום) ḳillus is stretching out the arms (and clapping), contrad to טיפוח.
